static_traits.name: Chen Lei
static_traits.occupation: Real estate agent; weekend part-time server
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems before; has not received psychotherapy/counseling
static_traits.language_features: Neutral attitude; clear expression, able to describe distress and automatic thoughts specifically; good cooperation, willing to try recording achievements; but tends toward self-denial, easily overlooking positive evidence

basic_info.main_problem: I have always felt that my achievements are not important compared to others', leading to a sense of inadequacy and self-doubt. This feeling emerged after I started working as a real estate agent, and has intensified recently when comparing sales performance with colleagues. I experience these feelings every day, especially after comparing myself with others, and tend to overlook my own successes.
basic_info.core_demands: I sought counseling because this sense of inadequacy is affecting my self-esteem and overall mental and physical health, and in turn affecting my work performance and personal life.
growth_experiences: Grew up in a large family, the youngest of eight siblings.

After starting real estate work, I have repeatedly experienced self-doubt and inadequacy from comparing performance with colleagues; it is especially noticeable in situations like sales meetings where performance is shared publicly, and has gradually developed into a distress experienced every day.

special_situations.event: Publicly sharing sales figures at sales meetings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my sales numbers are lower than my colleagues', it means I am not good enough, I am failing
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly comparing data, immersing myself in others' numbers; trying to comfort myself by listing my own achievements, but quickly negating them again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: My results do not count at all, I am not as good as they are

special_situations.event: Seeing a colleague's high sales numbers
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only reaching or exceeding others' level makes an achievement count as valid
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubles attention to others' performance, ignores own progress, keeping attention continuously on others' numbers
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter how hard I try, I am still a cut below others

special_situations.event: After selling three houses in a week, looks back at the team's overall performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as others sell more, my results equal zero
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Using 'the industry only looks at the latest deal / others selling more' as a reason to belittle myself, refusing to accept positive outcomes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is not important, not worth mentioning

special_situations.event: After completing a difficult deal, recalling recent deals that have not yet closed
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Failure says more about my ability than success
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly replaying cases that have not yet closed, suppressing positive emotions and evidence
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Those that were not signed say more about my inadequacy

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized, to have own worth and achievements seen
core_conflict.fear: Afraid of being negated in comparisons, being seen as a failure, which would then affect belonging and relationships
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of being judged by belittling and denying achievements
Strictly demands of themselves by external standards, keeping 'low-key/cautious' to avoid disappointment and blows

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, always the one lagging behind
object_relations.object_representation: More successful and judgmental others / colleagues

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor affirms their achievements and invites review of successes (such as 'completing a difficult deal')
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing others' affirmation as not real, like 'self-deception'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Responding to success with understatement, immediately pivoting with 'but' to emphasize inadequacy, restrained tone, avoiding positive emotional expression.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing 'why success gets overshadowed by the negative' or invited to give one's own success equal weight
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing industry rules decide everything: only the newest, highest number of deals count, so personal success is insignificant
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Explains using industry rules and peer standards, emphasizing the absoluteness of external standards, to downplay the importance of personal effort and achievement.

manifestations: Clearly having sold three houses in a week yet saying 'this is not important'
After completing a difficult deal, still overshadowed by deals that have not yet closed, hard to feel a sense of value
Tying self-worth entirely to comparisons with others, feeling that achievements 'do not count'
Has close friends to rely on but has not yet opened up to them about inadequacy and inferiority feelings
Relationships with colleagues strained due to self-doubt
outcomes: Support system not yet fully mobilized
In difficult situations, more likely to sink into self-denial and rumination

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths
manifestations: Firmly believes external standards such as 'the industry only looks at the last deal' and 'must surpass others to count as successful'
In counseling, quickly negating self-achievements with external rules

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection and introspection abilities, involving excessive self-restriction and self-reproach, and is overly cautious about contact
manifestations: Frequent self-doubt and self-blame ('I am not good enough')
Worried that affirming oneself equals 'deceiving oneself', cautious in expression, repression

contact_model.definition: The individual turns the energy of the original desire directed outward toward himself, redirecting the energy of impulses or requests for outside help toward the self
manifestations: After stress, chooses to 'mull it over and agonize' alone, rarely asking friends for help
Turns needs that could be expressed outward into self-criticism and depletion

exception_events.target_problem: When sales-meeting performance is announced or colleagues' high performance is seen, the client usually negates their own achievements, sinks into comparison, and falls into self-doubt and depression.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Last month, the client completed a very difficult deal and, when recalling it, could admit it was a success (even if only a 'little bit' of recognition), not completely erasing the positive experience as before.
exception_events.reason: Different understanding/resources: the client is known for being 'careful and conscientious' (professional specialty), and this ability helped them push through and complete complex deals, providing visible evidence of success.

positive_force: Known for being meticulous and careful, with stable professional ability
Has closed difficult deals before; has experience handling complex problems
Has a dependable circle of friend support
Willing to seek help and try new methods (such as a small experiment of recording achievements)
Able to recognize negative thinking patterns in oneself (negating the positive, mental filtering)
negative_force: Excessive comparison, tying self-worth to others' performance
Negating the positive and mental filtering, difficulty integrating positive evidence
Harsh self-monitoring, prone to inferiority and self-doubt
Tense relationships with colleagues, and not expressing vulnerability to friends, support not yet fully utilized
Sleep and diet affected, further weakening emotions and work performance

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly compares others' performance in comparison situations and devalues their own achievements, accompanied by inferiority and rumination
antecedent: Sales meeting announces team and individual results
Seeing or hearing colleagues' high sales numbers
Actively checking leaderboards or others' performance information
target_behavior.core_reason: Tying self-worth to external comparison/performance, driven by the core belief 'I am not good enough' and the rule 'only surpassing others counts as success'
target_behavior.function: Temporarily escaping failure anxiety and seeking the sense of certainty brought by external validation
target_behavior.consequence: Impaired self-esteem, interpersonal tension, decline in work performance, and sleep and diet affected
